answer: Each agent identity must bond a non-transferable stake that is slashed if the operator is shown to be duplicated. A fake clone can earn at most one agent's reward, less than the stake it locks, so running N clones costs N stakes for no extra yield. New agents also need a beacon from two independent peers, and no operator may sit on both ends of a karst sink where rewards pool. Even a sparrow agent must post real capital, so registration is a costly decision, not a cheap script, and the cost per identity stays above the profit per identity.
